observations.detail: Coinbase states its 2026 priorities are the everything exchange, stablecoins/payments and onchain adoption; it says the Circle arrangement was renewed on the same terms.

Q3 2026 net revenue was $1.2B, transaction revenue $590.2M, subscription/services $570.2M; transaction revenue fell 44% year over year. Consumer spot volume fell 59% and institutional spot volume fell 53%, with derivatives and prediction markets offsetting part of the decline.

Q3 stablecoin revenue was $306.905M versus $324.534M a year earlier. Coinbase says higher average USDC balances added $84.6M to Q3 stablecoin revenue, while lower average rates reduced it by $52.8M. Q3 average USDC held in Coinbase products was reported at $22B, up 49% year over year.

Coinbase says it renewed its Circle arrangement on the same terms. Circle's Q2 filing describes Coinbase compensation as allocations linked to USDC held on Coinbase after issuer retention plus half of certain broader ecosystem-growth amounts after approved third-party participant payments.
Circle reported $324.6M distribution costs connected with Coinbase agreements in Q2 2026 and $655.3M for H1 2026. These are Circle expenses, not Coinbase net profit or a direct XRP flow.
At 2026-09-30 Coinbase reported $1.976B total loan receivables: $1.959B fiat/payment-stablecoin receivables and $17.598M crypto-asset loan receivables. This does not disclose XRP-specific loans.

Recognized crypto lending collateral fair value was $997.557M: BTC $920.649M, ETH $67.005M and other crypto assets $9.903M. The filing does not identify XRP within the other-assets aggregate; if XRP is included, it cannot exceed that aggregate at the reported date.

Recognized derivatives collateral at 2026-09-30 totaled $301.943M and the disclosed table lists BTC and ETH, not XRP. This does not disprove product-level XRP collateral eligibility, but it does not evidence material XRP collateral utilization.

Coinbase separately reported $3.285B of borrower-pledged collateral it did not recognize as its own collateral/return obligation: $480.45M fiat/payment stablecoins and $2.804B crypto assets. Do not treat this as Coinbase-owned collateral or XRP utilization.
Circle says USDC is native on XRPL, no third-party bridge is required, Circle Mint/APIs support it, and qualified businesses can convert fiat directly into XRPL USDC and redeem 1:1 for USD.

Coinbase launched RLUSD on Prime, Exchange and retail on 2026-10-28. Deposits/withdrawals are supported on XRPL, Base and Ethereum. The announcement says Global Exchange collateral use will follow, and Ripple will provide Base liquidity.

Bitnomial announced XRP and RLUSD margin collateral for its regulated derivatives complex, subject to applicable regulatory approvals. Its current clearinghouse page lists XRP at a 40% haircut and $15M notional limit. This is venue/product-specific, not a universal CFTC classification.

The CFTC's 2025-12-08 digital-assets pilot initial three-month eligible list for FCMs relying on the no-action position was BTC, ETH and USDC. XRP was not on that initial list. The same release discusses tokenized real-world assets and risk controls.

Tokyo SBIC's official 2025-02-26 seminar was titled 'Current and Future of Generative AI (ChatGPT)'; it described ChatGPT and a Microsoft Japan speaker demonstrating usage. The PDF identifies Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. as organizer and describes the SME investment-development policy role. This is an educational event, not an OpenAI partnership or XRP connection.

SBIC West Japan / Osaka Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. published a 2025-12-04 seminar on generative AI including ChatGPT. Tokyo and Osaka are distinct regional legal entities; 'Japan SBIC' must not be treated as one unspecified corporation.

Permission Coin uses ticker ASK and official documentation lists Base and Polygon LayerZero OFT contracts. No XRP or XRPL integration is established by these sources. ASK is not a unique ticker, so this candidate is not confirmed as the user's intended 'ASK Coin'.

Indexed YouTube videos and a Glasp channel-summary page attribute XRP content to Kamilah Stevenson (channel ID UCqUPJMQdkCN6lsLVDnichPA); some transcripts self-introduce the speaker as 'Camila Stevenson'. This is a plausible candidate for the user's phonetic 'Camilla Stephenson' reference, but exact identity equivalence is not verified. Seven public video candidates are indexed; this is not an exhaustive channel archive.

Exact public searches for the phrase 'actual capital' with XRP, Kamilah/Camila, ASK and SBIC did not locate a verifiable source. A separate video title uses the word 'ACTUALLY' ('How Much XRP Do You ACTUALLY Need?'), but that does not establish the phrase 'actual capital' or the intended reference.

OCC granted preliminary conditional approval on 2025-12-12. Ripple's official October 26, 2026 press release says the OCC announced final approval that day; Ripple's October 28 event release repeats that final approval was received. The separate OCC final decision document and actual commencement date were not independently located in the OCC decision index captured in this run. RNTB's approved activities are reserve management, collateral trustee and fiduciary custody; RLUSD continues to be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company (SCTC), the NYDFS-regulated issuer. Classify final approval as Ripple-reported pending the OCC final order.

The 2025-12-14 video titled 'Ripple Just Became a BANK' was published two days after OCC's preliminary conditional approval. The OCC letter explicitly said final approval and authorization to commence business had not yet been granted. The title therefore overstated legal status at publication time. Ripple later reported final approval on 2026-10-28; that later issuer claim does not retroactively make the December title accurate.

PermissionDelegationV1_1 (XLS-75) activated on XRPL mainnet on 2026-10-08 at ledger 107524865, according to Unchained's ledger-referenced reporting. It replaces the earlier buggy amendment. It enables limited delegated permissions, not transfer of master-key control.

BatchV1_1 (XLS-56) activated on 2026-10-09 after fixBatchV1_2, according to XRPLinsights' ledger-referenced report. It supports atomic groups of transactions; implementation and network activation are distinct from any market-demand effect.

XRPLWin's snapshot around 2026-11-03 19:17 UTC showed ConfidentialTransfer (XLS-96) at 20 of 35 trusted validators (57.14%), below the more-than-80% threshold of 29 for 14 consecutive days. It was not active at that snapshot. XLS-96 applies to Multi-Purpose Tokens, not native XRP transfers.

The XLS-68 Sponsor amendment was not activated on mainnet as of XRPL.org's 2026-09-21 vulnerability disclosure. A reserve-accounting flaw was found during Devnet testing; the fix shipped in xrpld 3.4.0 on 2026-09-17. A dated 2026-10-17 vote snapshot reported Sponsor at 9/32 (28.1%), still below threshold. The 2026-11-04 fixCleanup3_4_0 activation window is a separate maintenance fix and does not itself activate Sponsor. Current Sponsor vote count was not independently retrieved in this run.

XRPLWin reported fixCleanup3_4_0 at 33/35 validators (94.29%), majority since 2026-10-21 14:46:22 UTC and scheduled for 2026-11-04 14:46:22 UTC if support remains above 80% continuously. It is a bundle of fixes, including sponsorship-related fixes; it is not the Sponsor feature amendment itself.

At the same approximate 2026-11-03 19:17 UTC snapshot, SingleAssetVault showed 21/35 (60%) and LendingProtocol 19/35 (54.3%), both below the 29/35 sustained threshold. These were not active at that snapshot.

A 2026-09-04 independent amendment-status analysis reported DynamicMPT at 15/35 validators (42.9%), below the 29-vote threshold. A current exact validator-vote snapshot was not retrieved in this run; current activation status remains unverified.

TokenPost reports Blockworks figures for Q3 2026: XRPL stablecoin supply rose 25.2% to $1.03B, RLUSD reached $1.01B (98.1%), and gross stablecoin transfer value reached $14.09B. The report explicitly says transfer value does not identify unique users or recurring commercial settlement. Treat these as gross network measures, not net new capital or XRP demand.

Bitquery's Oct 19 investigation of Sep 19-Oct 18 found 7.821M RLUSD payments; 7.789M (99.6%) came from a 110-wallet dust cluster sending about 0.00099 RLUSD per payment to three collectors, carrying only 7,722 RLUSD. The cluster paid 495 XRP in fees for 8.6M transactions and accounted for 45.6% of all XRPL account-to-account payments during Oct 8-14. Excluding dust, 14,600 payments of at least 1 RLUSD moved $7.33B; ten senders accounted for 82%, issuer mint/redemption loops were about one fifth, and one $424M round-trip pair added gross volume without net economic transfer. Bitquery inferred a coordinated automated cluster from shared funding/destinations and timing; operator identity and motive are unknown. The cluster tapered around Oct 14-16, near Cross River's Oct 15 announcement; causality is unknown.

stables.cool reported total XRPL USD stablecoins of $716.8M on 2026-11-01 21:05 UTC (RLUSD $711.8M, USDC $5.0M). XRPL.to's page captured around 2026-11-04 01:20 UTC reported 855.3M RLUSD, 67,960 holders, 101,818 trust lines, top ten accounts holding 82%, and $3.2M 24h exchange volume; its page says the supply refreshes hourly but does not display an exact capture timestamp. These are non-synchronous and potentially methodologically different snapshots; do not average or infer a precise net flow without direct issuer obligations and same-time ledger queries.

Cross River announced on 2026-10-15 that RLUSD on XRPL is integrated into its Core Operating System, with one API for business USD/RLUSD conversion, cross-border settlement, treasury movement and traditional ACH/wire/real-time rails. Cross River says availability is currently limited to certain states. No production transaction volume, active customer count or net settlement value was disclosed.

Standard Chartered announced RLUSD custody on XRPL is live for eligible clients through its DIFC Branch, regulated by the DFSA. It is also working with Ripple and LMAX Group on a planned RLUSD collateral integration and collateral-mirroring model; that collateral capability is not yet stated as live.

Ripple announced on 2026-10-27 that BNY's Digital Asset Custody platform supports XRP and RLUSD. BNY is RLUSD's primary reserve custodian. BNY intends to enable clients to mint/redeem RLUSD directly through BNY and is exploring tokenized trade finance with Ripple and C2FO; future activities remain subject to approvals.

C2FO and Ripple announced on 2026-10-27 that financing and settlement activity for C2FO Instant Pay will use XRPL with RLUSD settlement. C2FO's historical $520B+ working-capital access refers to its existing Early Pay programs, not Instant Pay throughput, committed capital or XRP purchases. Production launch, transaction volume, capital providers and XRP bridge use remain unknown.

The Ripple-commissioned Blockworks Q3 report, repeated by TokenPost, says Q3 stablecoin supply was $1.03B. XRP Breadcrumbs' October 1 reconciliation cites September 29 snapshots of $1.213B from DefiLlama and $1.19B from RWA.xyz. These are $160M-$183M higher (about 13.4%-15.1%) than the Q3 report figure. The cutoff dates are close but not identical, and the provider universes/methods are not reconciled. Treat $1.03B, $1.19B and $1.213B as separate provider observations; do not average or use them as a single canonical supply series.

CoinDesk's September 5, 2026 Q2 review reported average daily active XRPL accounts down 24% year over year, new accounts down 25%, and daily order-book traders down about 41%, while order-book trading volume rose 79%. Average tokenized-asset and RLUSD balances reached about $4.26B. This supports a concentration hypothesis (fewer accounts moving more value), not proof of broad retail adoption or XRP demand.

Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. and Osaka Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd. are regional SME investment/consultation entities that publish ChatGPT/GenAI seminars. SBI Holdings is a separate Japanese financial group with distinct subsidiaries and partnerships. No corporate affiliation between the reviewed SBIC entities and SBI Holdings was found in the reviewed official records. Do not conflate SBIC with SBI.

SBI investor materials report that SBI Group holds approximately 9% of Ripple equity as its largest external shareholder. SBI Group and Ripple jointly established SBI Ripple Asia; SBI Group holds 60% of voting rights and Ripple 40%. This is corporate equity/JV ownership, not SBI ownership of 9% of XRP supply.

SBI Remit states it began Ripple DLT remittances in 2017 and SBI investor materials identify its 2021 service as Japan's first international remittance using XRP as bridge currency. Later official materials describe expansion to Philippines, Vietnam and Indonesia. Public corridor-level XRP volume and net XRP inventory are not disclosed.

SBI Holdings and Circle Holdings established a joint venture in 2025 following a 2023 MOU focused on USDC circulation, banking relationships and Circle Web3 services in Japan. SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank separately disclosed a $50M strategic Circle equity investment, split $25M each. The cited joint-venture announcement does not specify the ownership split; do not assume 50/50 from this source.

SBI VC Trade registered as Japan's first Electronic Payment Instruments Service Provider in March 2025 and began USDC distribution. This is a Circle/SBI relationship separate from XRP bridge remittance.

SBI VC Trade launched RLUSD in Japan on 2026-06-24 following JFSA approval, as a Japanese electronic payment instrument classification. The launch supports RLUSD distribution, not proof of XRP bridge utilization or XRP collateral use.

SBI Group says it is a founding validator of Circle's Arc mainnet and plans to use USDC and JPYSC. SBI Shinsei Trust's JPYSC is a separate trust-type yen stablecoin; SBI disclosed about ¥20.1B outstanding on 2026-09-07, about ¥6.9B of lending applications and ¥10B of backing assets allocated to short-term Japanese government bonds. No direct XRPL/XRP bridge between JPYSC and Arc was established by these sources.

source_quality.primary_vs_secondary: SEC filings and regulator releases are primary for disclosed facts; issuer product pages are primary for what the issuer says it offers, not independent proof of usage; market-data providers are single-source observations; DailyCoin/Glasp/channel directories are secondary.
source_quality.independence_warning: Coinbase press release and Coinbase 10-Q are not independent sources. Circle SEC filing and Circle product pages are not independent sources. Bitnomial product pages and Bitnomial press releases are one operator's statements. Bitquery's on-chain clustering is a detailed third-party analysis, but the bot label is an inference from transaction patterns; do not attribute operator identity or motive. TokenPost's Q3 stablecoin figures cite Ripple-commissioned Blockworks research. XRPL.to asks data users to use its documented API for integrations; its page snapshot is not a substitute for direct ledger reconstruction.
source_quality.timestamp_warning: Market snapshots have exact provider timestamps. Event PDFs and filings have publication dates, not necessarily ingestion timestamps. Never substitute publication date for data availability time.

agent_exchange_contract.data_flow: Lawful public/authorized source -> timestamped immutable capture -> provenance/data-quality checks -> structured evidence packet -> independent platform task -> disagreement and minority-objection register -> causal hypothesis graph -> point-in-time feature store -> walk-forward evaluation -> shadow/paper evaluation.
agent_exchange_contract.disagreement_policy: No forced unanimity. Preserve minority objections and independent red-team findings. Resolve factual disputes by source quality, independence, temporal fit and reproducibility, not agent majority vote.
agent_exchange_contract.least_privilege_policy: Read-only by default; no credentials or private data in prompts; adapters must be separately authenticated and scoped; writes, deployments, submissions, merges and financial actions require explicit user approval.
agent_exchange_contract.adapter_status: Architecture designed; only ChatGPT-to-GitHub repository access was tested in this run. All other adapters remain unconnected or unverified.
